statement: Model duct routes with rectangular or circular segments, each carrying an MEP system, cross-section, offset and slope, with elbows and transitions generated automatically at the route nodes.

source.ref: Modeling with MEP tools > Basic modeling with MEP tools > Place MEP Route

superiority: Routing follows analytic flow rules and re-sizes downstream automatically.
notes: CORRECTED — read Place MEP Route and Route Segment Settings; segment shape is Rectangular or Circular only (no oval), and fittings are generated at nodes of a route rather than placed one by one. Acceptance sketch: Route 3 straight duct segments around a corner: elbow fitting inserted, centreline length equals sum within 1e-6.

statement: Model pipe routes with diameter, MEP system and slope, where elbows, branches and transitions appear automatically as nodes and connections are created.

source.ref: Basic modeling with MEP tools > Branches and Takeoffs

superiority: Gravity pipe slope maintained as a constraint during edits.
notes: CORRECTED — read Branches and Takeoffs; Archicad names these fittings elbow, branch and transition (not tee/reducer), and a new pipe started from an elbow converts it to a branch even at a different diameter. Acceptance sketch: Pipe run with a branch connection and a diameter change: one branch fitting and one transition are generated and the connected port diameters match.

statement: Model cable carrier routes with their own tables of dimensions, with elbows generated at nodes and display attributes taken from an MEP system of the cable type.

source.ref: Modeling with MEP tools > Route settings and Route Specifications > Route Specifications

superiority: Cable fill checks live against tray size.
notes: CORRECTED — read Route Specifications and Place MEP Route; cable carriers have dimension tables but no reference set, and no separate conduit or wire tool is documented. Acceptance sketch: Tray with horizontal bend inserts a bend with correct radius.

statement: When ending a route at a terminal, accessory or equipment, let the user step through alternative connection paths with the arrow keys and cycle overlapping ports with the Tab key.

source.ref: Basic modeling with MEP tools > Place Terminal, Accessory, or Equipment

superiority: Optimal routing by cost with clash avoidance against structure and other systems.
notes: CORRECTED — read Place Terminal, Accessory, or Equipment and Place MEP Route; help documents alternative-path selection, port cycling and Magic Wand routing from a polyline, but no free-space auto-routing with clearances (the superiority text is Dino's differentiator). Acceptance sketch: Connecting a route end to a terminal with two feasible paths: the up and down keys toggle between them and the committed route ends exactly at the chosen port.

statement: Place terminal, accessory and equipment elements from an MEP library, each with typed connection ports, sized to match the host route unless overridden, and attached to a route with one click.

source.ref: Basic modeling with MEP tools > Place Terminal, Accessory, or Equipment

superiority: Ports carry typed medium, flow and pressure data.
notes: CORRECTED — read Place Terminal, Accessory, or Equipment; classes are Terminal, Accessory and Equipment (including inline valves and coils); lights and panels belong to the separate electrical tools, and port flow data is not described on this page. Acceptance sketch: Equipment ports snap and connect to a duct at the expected connector position.

statement: A route connected to a standalone MEP object inherits that connection point's MEP system, and routes of different system types may be joined with a branch while each keeps its own system.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > MEP Systems

superiority: Network graph is explicit and queryable.
notes: CORRECTED — read MEP Systems and Branches and Takeoffs; inheritance at the connection point and mixed-system connections are documented, whole-network propagation is not (flow is accumulated per system from a chosen start point in the System Browser). Acceptance sketch: Connecting a route to equipment whose port belongs to supply air gives the route the supply air system; joining two routes of different systems leaves each system unchanged.

statement: Let the user flip the flow direction of an MEP element after placement so that its inlet and outlet ports and dependent calculations stay consistent.

source.ref: Place Terminal, Accessory, or Equipment > Flip flow direction

superiority: Directions computed from a solver.
notes: CORRECTED — read Flip flow direction and Set slope of MEP routes; arrow annotation of segments is not documented, only the flip command and a green slope-direction arrow in 3D and section. Acceptance sketch: Flipping an inline valve in a pipe run swaps its inlet and outlet ports and the calculation direction follows the new orientation.

statement: Resize selected duct routes to fit user limits on rectangular width and height, circular diameter and air velocity, reporting whether any element changed.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > Duct Size Optimizer

superiority: Calculations are open formulas the user can inspect and cite.
notes: CORRECTED — read Duct Size Optimizer; limits are min/max dimension and velocity ranges (pressure-drop limits not documented), and calculation functions need a cloud license. Acceptance sketch: Sizing for 0.5 m3/s at 5 m/s gives diameter 0.357 m within 1e-3.

statement: Compute pressure drop along paths and report critical path.

source.ref: MEP Designer: pressure drop and balancing

superiority: Includes fittings loss coefficients by catalogue.
notes: REJECTED: MEP Designer help (System Browser, Ventilation data, Hydronics data, Hydronics Optimizer) documents volume flow, velocity, mass flow, capacities and temperatures but no pressure-drop calculation or critical-path report; hydraulic calculation is delegated to the external CALHYDRA add-on. Acceptance sketch: Pressure drop along a straight duct equals the Darcy-Weisbach value within 2 percent.

statement: Detect and list collisions between MEP elements and building elements with volume and optional surface tolerances.

source.ref: Collaboration > Collision Detection

superiority: Clash results are issues linkable to BCF.
notes: VERIFIED — read Collision Detection; groups of elements are defined by criteria (e.g. MEP versus construction), results go to the Model Check Report, and a Collision Detection command also sits on the MEP toolbar. Acceptance sketch: Clash test between a duct and a beam returns the overlap volume.

statement: Convert selected MEP elements into opening elements where they cross walls, slabs, meshes, roofs or beams, with optional offset, shape choice and merging of nearby openings.

source.ref: Openings > Create Openings from Selection

superiority: Penetrations coordinate as issues with approval status.
notes: CORRECTED — read Create Openings from Selection; MEP elements are named as typical sources, with Automatic, Rectangular or Circular shape, an offset, keep-original option and lengthwise or sideways merge tolerance. Acceptance sketch: A pipe of diameter D crossing a wall with offset c makes an opening of diameter D+2c in that wall; two parallel pipes closer than the merge tolerance yield one merged opening.

statement: Add an insulation layer of a given thickness to duct and pipe routes, either uniformly for all parts of a route or separately per part.

source.ref: Route settings > Route Settings - Branch, Positioning, Insulation

superiority: Insulation counted in quantities by system.
notes: CORRECTED — read Route Settings - Branch, Positioning, Insulation and MEP Element Custom Settings; thickness is documented, a separate insulation material or lining is not. Acceptance sketch: Insulation 0.05 increases outer diameter by 0.1.

statement: Import and export route specifications (reference sets and tables of dimensions) as XML files so manufacturer-specific sizes can be shared between projects.

source.ref: Route Specifications > Import-Export Route Specifications

superiority: Catalogues open data format.
notes: CORRECTED — read Import-Export Route Specifications and CALHYDRA Connection; no built-in manufacturer catalogue browser is documented, manufacturer data arrives as downloadable route specification packages and library parts. Acceptance sketch: Export one dimension table to XML and import it into an empty project: every DN row and value is identical.

statement: List MEP elements in the interactive schedule using MEP parameters such as length, diameter, DN, insulation thickness and ventilation or hydronic data, and label or dimension route segments.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > MEP Listing Parameters

superiority: Live quantities by system and storey.
notes: CORRECTED — read MEP Listing Parameters, Ventilation Listing Parameters and Label, dimension, and list MEP elements; grouping totals by system is possible via listing parameters but is not spelled out. Acceptance sketch: Total length equals the sum of segments.

statement: Display MEP routes and elements in plan in one of four modes (projected, full including insulation, simplified excluding it, or schematic) selected per element type in the view options, with a per-element override.

source.ref: Documenting the MEP project > Model View Options for MEP elements

superiority: Representation chosen per view and discipline.
notes: CORRECTED — read Model View Options for MEP elements and Display of Route Element; the options are projected, full, simplified and schematic (no single-line/double-line wording), and schematic line colours come from the MEP system. Acceptance sketch: Switching ducts from projected to schematic in the view options changes only the plan graphic to a system-coloured schematic symbol and leaves the 3D geometry unchanged.

statement: Define MEP systems as project attributes bound to one route kind (ductwork, pipework or cabling), a fixed distribution-system category, and fills, lines and surfaces for plan, 3D and schematic display.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > MEP Systems

superiority: Systems carry standard medium properties.
notes: CORRECTED — read MEP Systems; systems are organised in folders, can be duplicated, and replaced when deleted so elements keep a valid attribute. Acceptance sketch: Changing the system colour recolours all elements of that system in plan and 3D.

statement: MEP modeling tools are available only with an Archicad Collaborate or Max entitlement, and the calculation functions additionally require a cloud license.

source.ref: Modeling with MEP tools (availability notices) and MEP System Browser

superiority: Included in all editions.
notes: CORRECTED — read Modeling with MEP tools, MEP System Browser and CALHYDRA Connection; notices cite Collaborate or Max and cloud licenses for calculations; market expansion in Archicad 30 is not documented. Acceptance sketch: Without the entitlement the MEP route tools are unavailable, and without a cloud license the System Browser and optimizer commands are disabled.

statement: Export MEP segments and fittings to IFC with the IFC type assigned from the element type or from a classification mapping, and import IFC distribution elements as parametric MEP elements where the data allows.

source.ref: Advanced MEP features and interoperability > MEP elements in IFC exchange

superiority: IfcDistributionSystem fully populated.
notes: CORRECTED — read MEP elements in IFC exchange and Built-in IFC Type Mapping (IFC chapter, AC30); built-in mapping gives duct segment to IfcDuctSegment, bend to IfcDuctFitting BEND, etc.; export of ports with system assignment is not documented. Acceptance sketch: An exported rigid duct segment maps to IfcDuctSegment with predefined type RIGIDSEGMENT and a duct bend maps to IfcDuctFitting with predefined type BEND.

statement: Open projects from Archicad 26 or earlier with their legacy MEP content shown as ordinary library objects to which new MEP routes can connect.

source.ref: Migrating to Archicad 30 > Migrating MEP elements

superiority: Automated migration with report of unconverted items.
notes: CORRECTED — read Migrating MEP elements; the MEP solution was renewed in Archicad 27, older routes open as plain GDL objects, and back-saving to 26 keeps the original MEP model but drops newer MEP elements. Acceptance sketch: Legacy routes open as non-parametric objects, a new route connects to one of them, and back-saving to the old version preserves the original legacy model unchanged.

statement: Generate elbows, transitions and branches automatically at route nodes with angle, bend-factor radius, transition angle and branch dimensions taken from route specification tables.

source.ref: Route Settings > MEP Node Settings

superiority: Fittings as parametric families.
notes: CORRECTED — read MEP Node Settings and Route Settings; fittings are sub-elements (nodes) of a route rather than independent elements; elbow radius uses a bend factor with minimum 0.6. Acceptance sketch: Elbow angle 90 gives expected centreline arc length.

statement: Model flexible duct and pipe segments by spline-style input between route ports, with no automatic transitions added at the ends.

source.ref: Basic modeling with MEP tools > Place MEP Route (flexible segments)

superiority: Length-driven flexible routing.
notes: CORRECTED — read Place MEP Route; flexible segments use spline input and connect to ports, and differing end dimensions must be resolved in the route; a length-driven flexible routing with bend count is not documented. Acceptance sketch: A flexible duct drawn between two ports ends exactly at both ports and no transition element is added at either end.

statement: Joining a duct or pipe onto an existing route inserts a branch and splits the route automatically, and a take-off element accepts a duct with an automatically created transition.

source.ref: Basic modeling with MEP tools > Branches and Takeoffs

superiority: Typed port schema shared with the library.
notes: CORRECTED — read Branches and Takeoffs; branches and duct take-offs are documented, multi-port manifold elements are not. Acceptance sketch: Connecting a pipe to the middle of a route splits it into separate route elements joined by one branch fitting with three connectors.

statement: Route settings provide defaults for the route and its segments and nodes, including MEP system, positioning, insulation and dimension tables, and flag any sub-element that deviates with custom settings.

source.ref: Route settings and Route Specifications > Route Settings

superiority: Typed properties editable in bulk.
notes: CORRECTED — read Route Settings; route is a hierarchy of main element, segments and nodes, any sub-element can be customised and the dialog signals custom values. Acceptance sketch: Changing diameter in settings updates connected fittings consistently.

statement: Define reference sets of nominal sizes for ducts and pipes and per-element-type tables of dimensions based on them, with duplicate, hide-empty-rows and clear-row operations that reassign affected elements.

source.ref: Route Specifications

superiority: Dimension tables are plain data files with validation of manufacturer ranges.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Route Specifications, Create Reference Sets, Set up Tables of Dimensions and Clear Row; cable carriers have tables but no reference set. Acceptance sketch: Clearing one DN row reassigns every element using it to the next larger DN and lists each affected element with its old and new DN.

statement: Optionally split duct, pipe and cable carrier runs into individual pieces within manufacturer minimum and maximum lengths, stretching a too-short leftover piece to the minimum and shortening the previous full piece.

source.ref: Documenting the MEP project > Use individual lengths for pipes and ducts

superiority: Piece lengths feed purchase lists with cut waste reported.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Use individual lengths for pipes and ducts; individual lengths can be labeled and scheduled. Acceptance sketch: A 4.1 m run with piece lengths between 1 and 2 m gives pieces of 2, 1.1 and 1.0 m, summing to the run length.

statement: Resize selected heating and cooling pipe routes to user-defined diameter and velocity ranges and report whether any element changed.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > Hydronics Optimizer

superiority: Solver also balances pressure and shows the sizing rationale per segment.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Hydronics Optimizer and Hydronic system calculation - Cooling Systems; cooling and 4-pipe systems supported in Archicad 30, cloud license required. Acceptance sketch: A pipe carrying flow Q with allowed velocity range vmin to vmax ends with a diameter D where 4Q/(pi D squared) lies inside the range, and equal min and max values force a fixed velocity.

statement: Add a ventilation or hydronic system to a browser by choosing its start element, then show per-element flow, velocity, capacity and temperature accumulated toward the start, flagging loops where flow cannot be computed.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > MEP System Browser > Ventilation data

superiority: Network solver reports loops and imbalance with explanations.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read MEP System Browser, Add MEP System to System Browser, Ventilation data and Hydronics data; velocity is flow over cross-section area. Acceptance sketch: Two terminals of 0.1 and 0.2 cubic metres per second on one branch give 0.3 at the system start, and a closed loop is marked as not computable.

statement: Check that supply and extract terminals or equipment placed in each zone meet the zone's required ventilation air flows, and list zones that fail in the model check report.

source.ref: MEP Systems and calculations > MEP Model Check for zone ventilation

superiority: Continuous background check with fix suggestions per zone.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read MEP Model Check for zone ventilation; terminals partly or fully inside the zone count, system role is set in a Model Quality panel. Acceptance sketch: A zone requiring 0.05 cubic metres per second supply with terminals totalling 0.04 appears in the report, and adding 0.01 of supply clears it.

statement: Detect broken logical connections in MEP systems, such as size mismatches after a copy or resize, and repair them by generating missing transitions for the selected elements.

source.ref: Editing MEP routes and elements > Resolve broken MEP connections

superiority: Repair runs continuously and previews each fix before applying.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Resolve broken MEP connections and Find open MEP connections; open connections are highlighted and can be managed as issues. Acceptance sketch: Connecting a copied 100 mm route to a 150 mm port leaves an open connection, and the repair command inserts one transition so no open connections remain.

statement: Set route segment slope during input in percent, degrees or rise over run, keep the slope when the elevation changes, let new branches inherit it, and show slope feedback in plan, 3D and section.

source.ref: Editing MEP routes and elements > Set slope of MEP routes

superiority: Slope is a constraint that is kept during all downstream edits and checked against minimum gradients.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Set slope of MEP routes; plan slope text appears only for slopes of 5 percent or less. Acceptance sketch: A 2 percent slope over 10 m gives a 0.2 m elevation difference, equal to an angle of 1.146 degrees within 1e-3.

statement: Group electrical devices into named circuits fed by electrical panels with phases, voltage and wiring type, and compute per-phase load and demand load using the demand factor of each device's load classification.

source.ref: Electrical Systems > Electrical Project Settings and Circuits

superiority: Full circuit sizing with cable and breaker checks.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Electrical Project Settings, Circuits, Electrical Panels and Labeling Electrical Panel; documented as a first, experimental electrical feature in Archicad 30. Acceptance sketch: A 40 VA device on a circuit using phases A and B adds 20 VA to each, and a 15 VA device with demand factor 0.8 adds 12 VA of demand load.

statement: Save any modelled 3D selection as a custom MEP part with connection objects and a subtype, and draw a custom 2D plan symbol for MEP objects with offset and scale adjustment.

source.ref: Advanced MEP features and interoperability > Create custom MEP part

superiority: Custom parts are parametric and carry typed ports defined in a visual editor.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Create custom MEP part and Create custom MEP symbol; related library authoring is described in Creating MEP Objects. Acceptance sketch: A saved part with a single connection is not offered as an inline subtype, while a part with two collinear opposed connections is.

statement: Exchange pipe system hydraulic calculations with an external hydraulic engine by classifying elements, exporting the project, and importing the calculated results to update nominal diameters of pipes and inline elements.

source.ref: CALHYDRA Connection

superiority: Built-in hydraulic solver removes the external round trip.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read CALHYDRA Connection and Additional improvements; needs a CALHYDRA license, classification system and manufacturer route specifications, reserved elements in Teamwork. Acceptance sketch: After importing results that change a pipe from DN 20 to DN 25, the pipe and its inline valves report DN 25 and the pipe schedule shows the new quantities.

statement: Render the architectural model transparent through a graphic override combination while modeling MEP, with per-element transparency set by graphic override rules.

source.ref: MEP Work Environment > Show transparent architectural model while modeling MEP

superiority: Visibility of disciplines is controlled by presets without layer management.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read MEP Work Environment and View MEP design in transparent architectural model. Acceptance sketch: With the override active, architectural elements render with the configured transparency while MEP elements stay opaque and selectable.
